vulnerabilities.title: Public `initialize` function allows arbitrary minting to any address
vulnerabilities.description: The `initialize` function is public and can be called by anyone. While there is a check for `_totalSupply == 0`, this still allows a front-runner to call it before the intended deployer. The function mints tokens to `msg.sender` (the front-runner), not to a pre-defined address. This allows an attacker to steal the entire token supply upon deployment.
vulnerabilities.location: function initialize(string memory _name, string memory _symbol) public

vulnerabilities.title: Public `initialize` function allows re-initialization and infinite token minting
vulnerabilities.description: The `initialize` function uses `_totalSupply == 0` as a check to prevent re-initialization. However, if `_totalSupply` is 0, anyone can call `initialize` to mint tokens. If the contract allows burning or if there's a way to reset `_totalSupply`, the function could be called multiple times. More critically, since it's not protected by an `initializer` modifier from OpenZeppelin's Initializable, it could potentially be re-called if the supply somehow reaches 0 again (e.g., through a vulnerability in transfer or burn logic).
vulnerabilities.location: function initialize(string memory _name, string memory _symbol) public

vulnerabilities.title: Missing `_beforeTokenTransfer` hook
vulnerabilities.description: The contract does not override the `_beforeTokenTransfer` function from OpenZeppelin's ERC20. This could be intentional, but if the project requires any pre-transfer checks (like pausing, blacklisting, or other restrictions), they are missing.
